headline: Pricing and productivity drive double-digit EPS growth
summary_short: Revenue rose 29.5% to $5.4B and adjusted EPS grew 28.6% to $1.80. North American truckload adjusted gross profit per shipment rose 17.0% on disciplined pricing.
summary_long: North American Surface Transportation volume grew about 3.5% against a 0.3% decline in the Cass Freight Shipment Index, the 14th straight quarter of outgrowth. Average headcount fell 10.4% and operating expenses rose 10.6%. Operating cash flow fell $151.3M on working capital as transportation rates rose. Cash returned to shareholders was $289.1M. Capital expenditures for 2026 are expected at $65M-$75M. The pending RXO acquisition is being prepared for integration.
confidence_notes: Adjusted gross profit, adjusted operating income and adjusted EPS are non-GAAP. Cash flow delta computed from the release's stated $151.3M decrease versus $275.4M a year earlier.

drivers.explanation: Higher pricing in truckload, ocean, LTL and air services and higher truckload volume.
Higher adjusted gross profit per transaction in truckload, ocean, air and LTL, plus higher truckload and LTL volume.
Unfavorable working capital changes driven by higher transportation rates; net operating working capital rose $267.4M sequentially.
CEO credits market share gains, disciplined revenue management and Lean AI productivity improvements.
